subject: Dedicated capacity RFI: GPU mix & reservation worksheet (Acme Enterprise)
messages:
From: Jamie Porter <jamie.porter@acme-enterprise.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-enterprise.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity questionnaire - Acme Enterprise

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for agreeing to take a look at our dedicated capacity RFI. Attached is the questionnaire our procurement team put together — mostly around GPU types, expected throughput (qps / tokens/sec), and reservation/commitment terms.

High-level context: Acme is planning a customer-facing generative assistant that will be GA in Q4. We expect a ramp over 12 months and need predictable unit costs and isolation (VPC). Primary concerns are latency SLOs for 95th p99 paths, and the ability to burst for seasonal events.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports:
- Per-tenant VPC isolation for Dedicated instances
- Tiered reservation with burst capacity and per-minute billing for bursts
- A recommended GPU mix for a mixed workload (short chat + longer instruction sequences)

Timeline: procurement needs your completed questionnaire and a ballpark for committed monthly cost by Thursday, Apr 21.

Attached: Acme_RFI_Dedicated_Questionnaire.pdf (7 pages)

Thanks,
Jamie Porter
Senior Vendor Manager
Acme Enterprise
procurement@acme-enterprise.com

--
Jamie asked: "What version of A100 do you size for?"
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Porter <jamie.porter@acme-enterprise.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire - Acme Enterprise

Jamie — thanks for the RFI and the clear timeline. We completed the questionnaire and are attaching a filled workbook plus a short GPU mix projection CSV. High-level answers below; the workbook has the line-item details you can drop into your procurement doc.

Attachments: Redwood_Completed_Dedicated_Questionnaire.xlsx, redwood_gpu_mix_projection.csv

Short answers / recommendations:
- VPC isolation: yes. Redwood Private/Dedicated supports customer VPC peering and private control plane options; audit logs and KMS integrations are available for Dedicated customers.
- Reservation model: we recommend a two-tier commit for Acme:
  - Base reserved capacity (monthly committed GPU-hours) sized to cover 65-75% of expected steady-state peak.
  - Burst pool (automatically billed per-minute) to handle seasonal peaks up to 2-3x base for brief windows.
- GPU mix (initial recommendation):
  - H100 80GB (performance-critical gen/long-seq paths): 6 nodes (for p99 latency targets at projected concurrency).
  - A100 80GB (cost-efficient high-throughput for batching short responses): 10 nodes.
  - L4 / T4 family or 8-bit quantized instances (inference-optimized) for cheap embedding/low-latency short-chat paths: 6 nodes.
  Quantities above assume: average seq length 256 tokens for chat, 1024 tokens for instruction-heavy requests on 20% of calls, and an initial target of 400 qps aggregate with spikes to 1200 qps during events. Exact counts are in the CSV.

Throughput & latency guidance:
- Target: 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for short-chat path (<=256 tokens), p99 <= 800ms for long-instruction flows (<=1024 tokens) under steady-state with the base reserved pool.
- KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts recommended — expect 20-40% token cost reduction on stable prompts.

Operational notes & assumptions:
- Model variants: we will propose fallbacks (quantized model variants) for non-critical routes to keep unit costs predictable.
- Autoscaling policy: aggressive scale-up (sub-minute) + conservative scale-down (5–10m) to prevent flapping.
- Security: SOC 2 evidence available; we can provide a dedicated access review for Acme's auditors.

Open clarifying questions (please confirm):
1) Expected percent of calls that must be streaming (token-by-token) vs non-streaming?
2) Peak sequence length distribution beyond the 1024 bucket? Any 2k+ long-running requests?
3) Desired uptime SLA (99.9% vs 99.95%) to size redundancy and cross-region reserves.

We can turn the workbook into a line-item pricing estimate once we have those clarifications. Happy to hop on a 30-min sizing call — propose Wed Apr 20 10:00am PT if that works.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions — Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

Marcus — thanks for the rapid turnaround and the workbook. A few quick answers to your clarifying Qs and an additional artifact attached.

Answers:
- Streaming vs non-streaming: ~30% streaming (real-time assistants), 70% non-streaming (single-response).
- Long requests: roughly 8% of calls exceed 1024 tokens; there are a handful of batch workflows that hit 2k tokens but they are off-peak and tolerable to queue.
- SLA: Procurement is aiming for 99.95% for customer-critical routes and 99.9% for non-critical.

Attached: Acme_expected_workload_snapshot.json (small workload sample)

Also — procurement asked for a ballpark committed monthly price for the base reserved pool sized to support 70% steady-state usage and a small burst buffer (as you recommended). Can you provide that by EOD Thursday (Apr 21)? Can you also confirm support for VPC peering and whether egress to a customer VPC is billed separately?

Jamie

- Neha: validate whether the recommended H100/A100 mix meets the p99 latency targets in our benchmarks for mixed streaming/non-streaming; flag any changes needed to meet 99.95% for critical routes.
- Laura: prepare the SOC2/KMS evidence packet and a one-pager on VPC peering and egress billing to attach to the proposal.

Notes/constraints:

- If we must hit 99.95% for critical routes, we should recommend cross-region standby capacity; call this out in the pricing as an add-on.
